pools.name: Chūnin Exam Hall
pools.cutoff: Part I: Chūnin Exams / immediate Konoha invasion period
pools.scope: Strong adult fighters associated with this period. These are not the five strongest examinees. Ordering within the top group is debatable.
units: Part I; snakes, sword and forbidden techniques. No later-body upgrades.
Part I; summons and standard ninjutsu. Do not import Shippuden Sage Mode feats.
Elder Third Hokage version, not hypothetical prime Hiruzen.
Part I taijutsu specialist; do not give him the war-arc Eighth Gate kit.
Part I Sharingan / Lightning Blade; no Kamui or double Mangekyō.
pools.alternative: If you mean exam contestants only: Gaara (Epic), Naruto (Epic, finals version), Sasuke (Epic, Chidori), Neji (Rare), Rock Lee (Rare, limited Gates). Lee/Neji and the top three are matchup-dependent.

pools.name: Loguetown
pools.cutoff: East Blue / Loguetown, before entering the Grand Line
pools.scope: Present-day visitors and fighters; exclude Roger's historical execution. Dragon is a provisional inclusion: this arc does not reveal enough of his combat ability to rank him confidently.
units: Provisional mentor/boss candidate. No invented confirmed Devil Fruit or wind move set.
Loguetown captain with smoke powers and seastone jitte; no later vice-admiral upgrades.
East Blue rubber-fighting version; no Gears or Haki.
East Blue three-sword style; no Asura, Enma or Haki.
East Blue kicking style; no Diable Jambe, raid suit or later enhancements.
pools.alternative: If only demonstrated local combat counts, leave Dragon unranked and use Buggy (Rare) as the fifth playable pack candidate.

pools.name: Jujutsu High
pools.cutoff: Season 1 Kyoto Goodwill Event / school attack
pools.scope: A strong shortlist from the event and its attacking/supporting cast, not a settled canonical top five. The training pairing is Yuji and Todo; Yuta belongs to a different roster decision.
units: Adult Season 1 version; adapt Infinity to counterable game mechanics.
Goodwill Event version; use the abilities demonstrated in this encounter.
Season 1 version; no later Shibuya final transformation.
Goodwill Event Boogie Woogie; no later prosthetic/vibraslap version.
Grade 1 supporting sorcerer. Exact ranking and a strict Season 1-only combat kit remain uncertain.
pools.alternative: For the student training theme instead: Todo (Epic), Yuji (Rare/Epic), Megumi (Rare), Toge (Rare), Maki (Rare, pre-awakening). Yuta should be a separately labelled JJK 0 version if you choose him.

pools.name: Mount Fujikasane
pools.cutoff: Opening training and Final Selection period, through episode 5
pools.scope: Early-arc shortlist including mentors and the selection boss. Giyu and Urokodaki are not Final Selection contestants. Early Kanao/Urokodaki relative strength is inferred, not settled by direct fights in these episodes.
units: Opening-series Hashira; no later mark or final-battle upgrades.
Retired mentor version; not an invented prime form.
Final Selection candidate; no later eye technique or endgame feats.
Final Selection Water Breathing; blue cloud haori. No Hinokami Kagura or mark.
Final Selection boss; grab/arm pressure, with a readable counter.
pools.alternative: If you want only the five surviving recruits: Kanao (Epic), Tanjiro (Rare), Zenitsu (Rare), Inosuke (Rare), Genya (Common). Their exact strength order cannot be established from Final Selection alone.

pools.name: Heavens Arena
pools.cutoff: 2011 anime Heavens Arena arc; before Yorknew
pools.scope: Five practical arc-associated combat candidates. Wing's full fighting strength is not shown, and Machi's brief appearance does not establish a reliable comparison; this is not an official ranking.
units: Heavens Arena Bungee Gum and trickery; no later manga developments.
Nen teacher. Full combat kit is unspecified; keep any game adaptation labelled as such.
Tiger Bite Fist and Double, as demonstrated against Hisoka.
Early assassin training and basic Nen; no electricity or Godspeed.
Heavens Arena basic Nen and physical fighting; no Jajanken or adult form.
pools.alternative: Zushi is a natural Common addition for the wider pack pool. A strict strongest-five list could include Machi, but her placement is uncertain.

pools.name: Wano
pools.cutoff: Onigashima raid resolution; exclude historical flashbacks and post-raid arrivals
pools.scope: Leading raid combatants. Strength ordering among Law, Kid, Yamato and other contenders is debatable. Using the Flower Capital arrival date instead would remove these later raid upgrades.
units: Wano raid version; keep base and hybrid forms explicitly labelled.
Gear 5 only if the arena pool covers the end of the raid. Otherwise use Gear 4.
Wano version with her homies; no invented post-Wano form.
Raid version; awakened abilities only under the end-of-raid cutoff.
Raid version; awakened magnetism only under the end-of-raid cutoff.
pools.alternative: Yamato is a credible substitution for Law or Kid. If the intended date is the Flower Capital arrival, use pre-raid versions and revisit the shortlist.

pools.name: Marineford
pools.cutoff: Opening frozen-bay battle, before Shanks's arrival
pools.scope: Five frontline powerhouses for the iced-over bay, not an uncontested verse ranking. Garp and Sengoku are strong alternatives; their exact order relative to these five is unsettled.
units: Old, ill Marineford version; not prime Whitebeard.
Marineford swordsman; no later bounty-based scaling.
Pre-timeskip admiral; no post-timeskip fleet-admiral assumptions.
Pre-timeskip admiral and the bay's ice theme; not post-Punk Hazard appearance.
Pre-timeskip admiral; no later Egghead feats.
pools.alternative: If the whole war is included, Shanks becomes eligible. Garp and Sengoku also belong on the wider strongest-candidate list.

confirmed: Dragon Ball / Z / Super character choices come from you.
Story arena completions unlock additional character pools; a gift unit is separate from pack eligibility.
Cash earned through play buys packs; obtained units enter inventory and can be equipped into a team.
Both ranked and unranked PvP unlock after Arena 3.
Mystical units are excluded from normal arena packs. Intended sources: a rotating weekly Robux store or ranked rewards.
The season pass has 45 levels; you will supply rewards and UI artwork.
Top-100 ranked players should receive the selected Mystical unit plus other rewards such as XP cards / pack rewards.
proposed: Use 5 Season XP for a completed win and 2 for a completed loss, with 15 XP per reward tier. Monthly pass reset; daily tasks can refresh separately.
Use story completion flags to group progression, and ranked trophies to measure PvP results. Story wins should not inflate competitive trophies.

Treat season ranked wins as a separate leaderboard counter. Provisional simplest launch: global top 100 eligible players by ranked wins, with trophy total then head-to-head or earliest achievement as published tie-breakers.
To reduce farming weaker opponents, use the highest league reached this season for reward eligibility, rating-based matchmaking, repeat-opponent limits and server-validated completed matches.
Example trophy movement only: +20 for an even-rated ranked win, -15 for a loss, zero change for unranked. Tune after playtesting; do not ship these numbers as confirmed rules.
Keep Mystical units within the same competitive power budget as top earnable units, with distinctive abilities/appearance. A rotating paid unit should not be required to compete.
pending: Arena participants versus strongest known in the wider verse; provisional lists use each arena's story period.
5 XP per win / 2 per loss versus the later 5 / 10 wording.
Does top 100 mean global or top 100 within every league? Per-league distribution creates far more winners and needs anti-deranking rules.
Which modes award Season XP, whether story replays have caps, and whether draws grant anything.
Trophy gain/loss values, league thresholds, matchmaking rules and the monthly trophy reset/soft-reset policy.
Whether rank rewards are based on most wins or final trophies. The draft preserves your most-wins idea as a separate leaderboard.
Cash amounts, pack costs/odds, gift units, mastery rewards and XP-card purpose.
45 earnable rewards from tier 0 (675 XP), or start at level 1 with only 44 advances (660 XP).
Weekly store rotation time, price, reward unit schedule, late claims and duplicate Mystical compensation.
steps: Short loading screen → optional guided first fight
Play Story Arena 1 with a starter team
Receive any first-clear gift and unlock that arena’s pack pool
Spend cash on eligible packs → collect units → equip up to the game’s existing team size
Complete Arenas 2 and 3; continue story, mastery and team upgrades
Arena 3 clear unlocks Unranked and Ranked queues
Ranked results change trophies and add ranked wins; eligible completed matches add Season XP
Claim pass tiers during the month; settle ranked rewards at season end; rotate the Mystical store weekly

screens.title: PvP hub
items: Ranked: current league, trophy total, progress to next league, season wins and countdown.
Unranked: practise with no trophy gain or loss; show whether Season XP/cash is enabled once decided.
Before Arena 3: both queue buttons explain the unlock requirement and offer Continue Story.
After Arena 3: separate Find Ranked Match and Find Unranked Match buttons.

screens.title: Ranked queue / results
items: Queue: team check, opponent search status, elapsed time and Cancel.
Before match: own/opponent league and a readable team summary; no misleading guarantee of identical unit collections.
Results: outcome, cash, Season XP and trophy change as separate rows; ranked-win counter updates only after a validated win.
Leaderboard: clearly label global versus league scope, season identifier, tie-breakers and top-100 reward preview.

screens.title: Season pass / store
items: Pass: current tier / 45, XP progress, monthly end date, claim states and reward slots supplied by you.
Daily challenges, if added, show their own reset timer; they do not wipe monthly pass progress.
Store: show the current Mystical unit, fixed Robux price, weekly rotation timer and ownership state.
Rank rewards: show qualifying finish, claim deadline and duplicate policy once chosen.
